The name and the form have an older use: pandeiro once meant a square double-headed frame drum, often with a bell inside, now mostly called adufe in Spain and Portugal; Galicia, Asturias and parts of Portugal still use the name for a square drum, while the round drum with jingles is called pandeira or pandeireta there. The pandeiro is the common hand-held frame drum of Brazil, a membranophone by sounding classification, H-S number 211.311+112.122. Its head can be tuned, the rim carries cup-shaped metal jingles, and its timbre is brighter, drier and shorter in sustain than the tambourine's. It is played holding the drum in one hand while the other alternates thumb, fingertips, heel of the hand and palm on the head, and the body can be shaken or the fingers slid across the head to make a roll. It is commonly used in Brazilian samba, choro, coco, capoeira and bossa nova and other music.
潘德羅框鼓框體採用優質木材製造，通常選用桃花心木或其他硬木以增強共鳴效果。鼓膜為: The frame of the pandeiro is made of good wood, usually mahogany or another hardwood, to increase resonance. The head is animal skin, mostly goatskin or cowhide, and its tension can be adjusted to change the pitch. The frame carries several pairs of metal jingles (platinelas), usually of bronze or brass and cup-shaped. The grip is shaped in wood for comfort in one hand. The whole structure fuses Portuguese, African and Indigenous instrument-making craft.
潘德羅框鼓音色明亮清脆，具有乾爽的質感，音域屬於中高頻段，音程短暫而富有穿透力。: The pandeiro has a bright, dry timbre in the middle and upper frequencies, with short notes that carry. The sound comes from the head and the metal jingles together: the silvery ring of the jingles blends with the stroke on the head to make a layered sound. Next to the pale sharpness of the tambourine the pandeiro has more warmth and body; next to the deep African drums it is lighter and more mobile. The tunable head lets the player set the pitch as needed, so the drum can both mark the rhythm clearly and give fine detail in fusion music. These resonating qualities make it an indispensable rhythm instrument in Brazilian music.
